1.explanation: The file src/languages/elixir.js defines the numeric literal patterns for Elixir. Its current regular expressions omit standalone zero and numbers with a leading zero, so "0", "0123" and floats like "0.3" aren’t fully matched by the number mode. To fix this bug, the number‐matching regex in this file must be updated to allow zero and leading‐zero numerals.
1.bug_scenario:
When using highlight.js to highlight Elixir code, the literal “0” on its own is not recognized as a number, nor are integer or float literals that begin with 0 (for example “0123” and “0.3”). In the screenshot you can see that:  
  • “0” is left unhighlighted.  
  • “0123” is not highlighted at all.  
  • “0.3” only has the “3” highlighted.  
All of these are valid Elixir numeric literals and should be highlighted as numbers.

2.explanation: The Elixir language definition (src/languages/elixir.js) contains the numeric regex pattern that drives number highlighting. It currently only matches integers and floats starting with [1-9], omitting “0” or any digit sequence beginning with 0. To fix this bug, adjust the numeric matching rule in elixir.js to include “0” as a standalone integer, allow leading zeros in decimal integers, and correctly parse floats with a leading zero.
2.bug_scenario: In Elixir code blocks the literal “0” and other numbers starting with zero (e.g. “0123”, “0.3”) are not being recognized as numeric tokens by highlight.js. As a result, “0” is left unhighlighted, “0123” receives no number highlighting at all, and in floats like “0.3” only the “3” is treated as a number. All valid Elixir integer and float literals beginning with 0 should be highlighted.
